claude.note: Table 2 prints two FKC rows for gamma 40, N 32. Left block: CLIP 29.00, IR 0.04. Right block: CLIP 29.14, IR 0.05. The CFG row is 28.75, -0.24 in both. astra.headline: right
astra.note: 29.14 and 0.05 is the right-hand block of Table 2, which is FKC batch size 8 (pages 38 and Table A3). The row does not state the batch size.

joint_evidence: The product of two diffusion models is built from their separate scores (Prop. 3.3, p5). The dual-target molecule runs use no joint training data (p8, p39).
serves: problem 1: method only. The product is shown on molecules, the image runs are single-condition CFG, and no run composes two image concepts from separate models
best_idea: Adds Feynman-Kac importance weights to a diffusion sampler and resamples particles so samples track an annealed, geometric-mean or product target built from pretrained score models.
best_headline: EDM2 on ImageNet-512, gamma 40, N 32, 10,000 images: EDM2+CFG CLIP 28.75, IR -0.24; EDM2+FKC CLIP 29.00, IR 0.04 at batch size 32 and CLIP 29.14, IR 0.05 at batch size 8

claude.headline: right
claude.note: Table 1: O-O BLIP-VQA 0.7503 RTD, 0.5146 CO3; A-O 0.8422 RTD, 0.8878 CO3. The multiplier checks: 0.7503/0.5146 = 1.458. The footnote to Table 4 says its CO3 and SDXL results are copied from the CO3 paper, and Table 1 prints the same CO3 BLIP-VQA values.

joint_evidence: A single prompt containing all K target concepts drives the pilot attention pass and the sampling (section 3.1 on p2, Algorithm 1 on p4). No training.
best_idea: Runs one pilot pass to get each concept's attention map, then makes one norm-bounded update to the starting noise that reduces overlap between the maps, and samples normally.
best_headline: AE-Bench object-object prompts on SDXL: BLIP-VQA 0.7503 for RTD against 0.5146 for CO3 (45.8% higher) and 0.6440 for ToMe, the best other method (16.5% higher)
